summary:
AFTERLIGHT is an interactive, cinematic 3D space archaeology archive documenting the rovers, landers, and scientific instruments left silent across the Moon and Mars. Built with Next.js, TypeScript, Three.js / React Three Fiber, and Tailwind CSS, it transforms static planetary telemetry into an immersive digital museum.

Space exploration data is often scattered across technical catalogs, making it difficult for the public, students, and researchers to visualize humanities' physical footprint beyond Earth. AFTERLIGHT solves this by combining high-fidelity 3D planetary globes, true-to-life coordinate mapping, and scroll-driven storytelling. Users can rotate planetary horizons, inspect hardware components via interactive 3D hotspots, examine verified timelines, and link engineering innovations directly to scientific breakthroughs.


These silent machines mark humanity’s boldest scientific milestones, yet they sit motionless in extreme, deteriorating alien environments. AFTERLIGHT preserves their memory with verified, classroom-safe historical records and primary mission citations (NASA, NSSDCA, ESA, ISRO, LROC, HiRISE). By treating these artifacts with archaeological dignity, it inspires the next generation of engineers and space explorers while safeguarding our shared off-world heritage
details:
AFTERLIGHT — Digital Space Archaeology Archive

AFTERLIGHT is an immersive digital archive that preserves the stories, engineering, and exact resting places of historical robotic explorers on the Moon and Mars.

1. Core Features

  • Dual-World Exploration: Switch between photorealistic 3D Moon and Mars globes.
  • Precision Landing Sites: Explore verified landing coordinates through interactive planetary maps and cinematic camera descents.
  • Mission Storytelling: Discover each mission through scroll-driven chapters, from launch to its final transmission.
  • Interactive Hardware: Rotate 3D rover models and inspect engineering components through interactive hotspots.
  • Engineering to Discovery: Understand how hardware innovations enabled scientific breakthroughs.

2. Key Benefits

  • Converts complex space mission data into engaging stories.
  • Makes aerospace engineering accessible to students and the public.
  • Provides fact-checked information backed by NASA, JPL, ESA, and other primary sources.
  • Delivers an accessible, responsive, and optimized experience.

3. Intended Impact

  • Digitally preserves humanity's extraterrestrial heritage.
  • Inspires interest in STEM and aerospace engineering.
  • Connects people emotionally with the machines that explored distant worlds.

4. Technology Stack

  • Frontend: Next.js, React 19, TypeScript
  • 3D Graphics: Three.js, React Three Fiber, Drei
  • Styling: Tailwind CSS
  • Animations: Framer Motion
  • Validation: Zod
  • Backend: Express.js, PostgreSQL, Prisma
  • Storage: Supabase, Cloudflare R2
  • Data Sources: NASA, JPL, NSSDCA, LROC, HiRISE

5. Creative Approach

  • Space archaeology as the central storytelling concept.
  • Minimalist, cinematic dark-space aesthetic.
  • Persistent 3D canvas for seamless planetary exploration.
  • Last Transmission: A dedicated experience highlighting each machine's final communication.

6. Development Considerations

  • Historical accuracy and verified planetary coordinates.
  • Performance optimization through adaptive rendering.
  • Accessibility, keyboard navigation, and WCAG AA compliance.
  • Modular architecture for easily adding future missions.
